method: Highest-conviction dossiers as of the Fri 2026-09-25 close, ranked by conviction then composite score. Levels are anchored to each name's real 52-week range.

ideas.why: Record $60.9bn of AI orders and a $95bn backlog, and the stock just reclaimed +5% on Friday after pulling back from a 595.51 high. It is flat over two weeks, which means the fundamentals have caught up to the price.
bull: Record $60.9bn of AI server orders; backlog at $95bn
Morgan Stanley raised the odds on a $756 bull case
FY sales guide raised to $192bn
bear: Thin gross margin on AI servers: backlog dollars convert to far less profit
+410% off the 52-week low — crowded
Oracle's Project Jupiter force-majeure notice shows AI-buyer financing can wobble
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks if hyperscaler/neocloud capex is cut or backlog conversion slows.
ideas.thesis: A- (81.9/100). It pulled back 5.5% from the 595.51 high and bounced hard on Friday. Accumulate near ~540.37 if that bounce is retested and holds; a close above 595.51 is the breakout add. Keep size modest — it is still +410% off its low.

ideas.why: Muse is the first consumer AI agent to beat ChatGPT on the App Store, and it moved the whole chip complex on Sep 21. Five brokers raised targets; the stock is up 16% in two weeks and sits 3.6% under its high.
bull: Muse topped the US free iOS chart ahead of ChatGPT within two weeks
JPMorgan $920 and Canaccord $950 targets
Ad engine self-funds the AI build
bear: +16% in two weeks — Friday's -3.33% may not be the end of the digestion
Muse has no revenue yet
Capex guidance could jump again
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks if Muse engagement fades or capex outruns ad growth.
ideas.thesis: A- (80.8/100). Friday's -3.33% is the start of the digestion you want. Accumulate near ~721.59 if the pullback holds there; don't chase back through 779.82 until Muse monetisation is visible.

ideas.why: Enterprise AI is standardising on Microsoft: Copilot passed 30 million paid seats, Azure is growing 43%, and Friday's +3.66% came with two target raises in three days.
bull: Copilot above 30 million paid seats; agentic Cowork now built in
Azure growth 43%
Stifel upgrade to Buy ($575) and Oppenheimer $570
bear: Still 6.8% under its high — Friday's gap can fill
AI capex intensity pressures free-cash-flow margins
A 5%+ 10-year compresses even quality multiples
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks if Azure growth decelerates sharply or Copilot seat growth stalls.
ideas.thesis: A- (80.3/100). Accumulate near ~500.68 on a pullback that holds the Friday gap; a close above 553.72 (the 52-week high) is the confirmation add. This is a build-over-weeks core name.

ideas.why: Trading under 17x forward earnings, near its lowest multiple in a decade, while the customers keep adding capacity: Colossus 2 alone plans up to 660,000 more GB300s by year-end. It is 4.8% below its 236.54 high with the chip index at records.
bull: JPMorgan lifted its target to $320 from $280; consensus average ~$324
Under 17x forward earnings — near the lowest multiple in over a decade despite +105.9% revenue growth
Colossus 2 is adding 220,000 GB300s next week and another batch in November
bear: Lagged the chip rally: +0.22% Friday while AMD printed a record and passed $1T
A 10-year yield at 5.17% compresses every long-duration multiple, even cheap ones
Customer concentration: a handful of hyperscalers and AI labs drive the order book
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks if hyperscaler capex guidance is cut, or on a close below the 200.31 stop.
ideas.thesis: B+ (77.2/100). It sits 4.8% under its 236.54 high, so the risk/reward from here is modest. Accumulate near ~218.32 on a pullback that holds, or add on a daily close above 236.54 with semis still leading; avoid adding the day before Micron's Sep 30 print.

ideas.why: Earnings in three sessions with the highest expected growth rate in its history. The stock has already rebounded ~17% into the print, so the set-up is about the gross-margin guide, not the headline beat.
bull: Revenue expected ~$51bn, +353% y/y — the largest growth rate on record
HBM sold out for 2026 and HBM4 shipping into Vera Rubin
Cantor $2,000, KeyBanc $1,750 and Citi $1,300 targets all raised this month
bear: A gross-margin guide below ~86% is the bear trigger analysts are watching
Memory pricing mean-reverts; DRAM spot is already up 52% since January
Up ~17% into the print — expectations are high
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks on a gross-margin guide that steps down materially on Sep 30, or on a close below the 952.41 stop.
ideas.thesis: B+ (77.1/100). Binary event on Sep 30. Either stay small into the print, or wait: if the gross-margin guide holds above ~86% and the stock holds the gap, accumulate near ~1049.81; if the guide steps down, let it find a floor first.

ideas.why: The market's new AI-compute co-leader: a $1T valuation reached on Sep 21 on the Meta Muse-driven chip rally, and a record close of 630.63 on Friday, 1.3% under its 639 intraday high.
bull: First close above $1T market value on Sep 21 — fourth US chipmaker to get there
Q2 revenue +50% y/y to $11.54bn with AI accelerators the growth engine
Record close 630.63 on Friday: trend, momentum and leadership all aligned
bear: +22% in two weeks leaves it extended — a normal 10% pullback is well within range
Second-source status means pricing power sits with Nvidia
Momentum names are first to be sold if the 10-year pushes through 5.2% again
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks on a close below the 554.95 stop or if MI-series share gains stall in the next guide.
ideas.thesis: B+ (76.6/100). Do not chase a stock 1.3% off its record after a 22% two-week run. Wait for a pullback toward ~605.4 that holds on volume, or a first higher-low after the Micron print on Sep 30; scale in, don't lump in.

ideas.why: A defensive leader in the one non-tech group making highs: the post-Humira transition worked, and the stock is within 2% of its peak. Added to the book this week.
bull: Skyrizi and Rinvoq growth replaced Humira
Healthcare is a new leadership group
Dividend plus buyback support
bear: 1.9% off the high — little margin of safety
Drug-pricing policy
Rate-sensitive dividend proxy
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks on a pricing shock.
ideas.thesis: B (73.9/100). Near its high: accumulate near ~253.77 on a pullback, or add on a close above 269.39.

ideas.why: The toll-road on AI silicon: whichever designer wins (NVDA, AMD, custom ASICs) the wafers come from TSMC. Up 4% in two weeks and 5.9% off the high with the chip complex at records.
bull: Every AI accelerator design — merchant or custom — runs through its leading-edge nodes
VIS's new Singapore fab was largely booked at start of production, a read on AI demand
Net cash balance sheet funds capex without dilution
bear: Taiwan geopolitical risk cannot be diversified away inside one stock
Capex intensity rises every node
A US-China trade setback would hit the supply chain first
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks on a cut to AI accelerator wafer guidance or a Taiwan Strait escalation.
ideas.thesis: B (73.7/100). Core holding, not a trade. Accumulate near ~432.59 on any dip that holds; a close back above 479 would confirm the next leg. Taiwan headline risk argues for building over weeks rather than in one order.

ideas.why: The quality way to own AI networking: near its high, holding gains through the Sep 16 hike and the yield spike, and less crowded than the server names.
bull: Ethernet is winning AI back-end networks as clusters scale
Held within 4% of its high through the Sep 16 hike and the 5.2% 10-year spike
Net cash, high margins, founder-led execution
bear: Premium multiple leaves little room for a guide miss
Hyperscaler concentration
Custom silicon from Broadcom and in-house designs competes for switch sockets
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks on a hyperscaler capex cut or loss of a major AI back-end design.
ideas.thesis: B (73.4/100). Close to its high, so patience. Accumulate near ~198.29 on a pullback that holds, or add on a daily close above 214.89 with the AI hardware group participating.

ideas.why: The value way into AI servers: a raised FY26 guide on 34-37% revenue growth, trading near its high at a far lower multiple than Dell. Added to the book this week.
bull: FY26 EPS guide raised to $3.75-3.85 on 34-37% revenue growth
Named alongside Dell as an Oracle AI-capex beneficiary
BofA target $88
bear: +217% off the 52-week low of 19.84
Lower margin than Dell with less AI backlog visibility
Juniper integration risk
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks on a guide cut or a close below the 55.39 stop.
ideas.thesis: B (73.4/100). Near its high. Accumulate near ~60.42 on a pullback that holds; a close above 65.65 is the breakout add. Size small — it is +217% off its low.

ideas.why: A US-China agreement that shelters US agricultural exports is a direct demand signal for farm equipment, and Deere is already near its high.
bull: US-China deal carves out US agricultural products
Precision-ag software raises margin through the cycle
Near its 52-week high
bear: Farm incomes remain cyclical
Finance-arm costs rise with rates
Deal details could disappoint
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks if the trade details exclude grains/soy or a close below the 614.51 stop.
ideas.thesis: B (72.7/100). Monday's US-China detail release is the trigger: if ag exports are confirmed, accumulate near ~662.84 on any pullback; a vague release means wait.

ideas.why: The Fed did hike, and a positively sloped curve (10y 5.17% vs 2y 4.81%) is good for NII — yet JPM slipped 3.7% as money chased tech. Q3 earnings in mid-October are the catalyst.
bull: Curve now +36bp 10s/2s — better for NII than any time this cycle
Fortress capital and deposit base
Q3 results in mid-October should show the hike
bear: Financials lagged all month
Higher-for-longer can surface credit losses
Investment-banking peers flagged softer trading (see GS)
ideas.inv: Thesis breaks on rising credit costs in Q3.
ideas.thesis: B (71.0/100). Accumulate near ~332.77 into Q3 earnings if it holds above 335; a close above ~357 (its Sep 11 close, before the hike) confirms the trend is back.
